item.title: How-to: Forcing HDMI Configuration on RK3568
item.description:
How-to: Keep HDMI Connected No Matter What

Schematic:

Analysis: Not controlled by GPIO

  • Setting either hpd-state or force_hpd has no effect.
  • Using display-timings also doesn’t work.
  • The next step would be to consider changing the cmdline… this seems to be the only available method.

Solution (Successful)

Open kernel/drivers/gpu/drm/bridge/synopsys/dw-hdmi.c Modify the function dw_hdmi_phy_read_hpd Change it to the following:

enum drm_connector_status dw_hdmi_phy_read_hpd(struct dw_hdmi *hdmi,void *data)
{
	// return hdmi_readb(hdmi, HDMI_PHY_STAT0) & HDMI_PHY_HPD ?
	// connector_status_connected : connector_status_disconnected;
	return connector_status_connected;
}

How-to: Force HDMI Resolution

item.title: LCDs (LVDS) Bring-Up on RK3568: A Study of the Data Flow
item.description:
Background Knowledge

  • Reference: How-to: Display Interface Debugging Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
  • Reference: Analysis of Key Concepts in the Rockchip Display Subsystem
  • Example: Using LVDS as a case study

Data Flow - (Hardware Perspective)

  • Okay, this step is to determine the hardware connections. Let’s directly map out the entire data flow.

1. Data from Memory -> VOP
